claims.statement: For every eligible ordinary tree T and p, if the selected sum S(T,p) is positive, then some original favorable leaf tag v and some independent (p-1)-set A of H_v meeting W_v have at least p vertices addable in H_v. Consequently, if every such marked set for every selected tag has at most p-1 addable vertices, then S(T,p)<=0.
claims.scope: Conditional necessary criterion for positive witnesses and sufficient obstruction to positivity under the stated addability bound; it preserves the exact original selector and tag multiplicities. It does not resolve the primary target.
claims.reason: An exact marked-incidence count on each bipartite forest H_v gives (p-1)S=(2a+1-3p)Q-E. Nonnegative per-set deficits then show that positivity forces one deficit below 2a+1-3p, which is equivalent to at least p addable vertices. The report proves alpha(H_v)=a-1 and checks the selector and rank domains.

limitations: This structural condition does not imply that a positive complete aggregate exists; deficits over other marked sets and selected leaf tags can compensate.
No reduction by pruning, grafting, support merging, or path compression is proved to preserve alpha, the first strict descent x, p eligibility, and the fixed favorable selector.
No counterexample or proof of the primary aggregate inequality is supplied.
